# Preparation

We first load all relevant packages and data.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(brms)
library(pander)
library(parameters)
library(bayesplot)

seed <- 395013

# load data
df_meta <- readRDS(here::here("output", "meta", "combined.rds"))

# Make passes TRUE when the upstream combined results changed
# and direct renders reuse cached fits
# params only exists during knitr rendering, fall back to FALSE interactively
refit_models <- isTRUE(if (exists("params")) params$refit_models else FALSE)

# the cache file names outlive likelihood changes, so a stale cache would otherwise load silently
read_fit <- function(path, family) {
  fit <- readRDS(path)
  stopifnot(stats::family(fit)$family == family)
  fit
}

# the response as the model sees it, e.g. log(rel_mse) for the Student-t models
model_y <- function(fit) brms::standata(fit)$Y

# coord_cartesian zooms without dropping draws, so the densities still use all of them.
# widen: margin around the observed range, as a multiple of that range
ppc_density <- function(y, yrep, group = NULL, widen = 0.25) {
  limits <- range(y) + c(-1, 1) * widen * diff(range(y))
  p <- if (is.null(group)) {
    bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay(y, yrep)
  } else {
    bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay_grouped(y, yrep, group = group)
  }
  p + ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = limits)
}

q01 <- function(x) stats::quantile(x, 0.01)
q05 <- function(x) stats::quantile(x, 0.05)
q95 <- function(x) stats::quantile(x, 0.95)
q99 <- function(x) stats::quantile(x, 0.99)

# log_y: compare on the log scale, for the lognormal S1 whose response is rel_mse itself
prior_check <- function(fit, log_y = FALSE) {
  y <- model_y(fit)
  yrep <- brms::posterior_predict(fit, ndraws = 50)
  if (log_y) {
    y <- log(y)
    yrep <- log(yrep)
  }
  ppc_density(y, yrep, widen = 1)
}

posterior_checks <- function(fit, log_y = FALSE) {
  y <- model_y(fit)
  yrep <- brms::posterior_predict(fit, ndraws = 500)
  if (log_y) {
    y <- log(y)
    yrep <- log(yrep)
  }
  group <- fit$data$model
  print(ppc_density(y, yrep[1:50, ], group = group))
  print(bayesplot::ppc_stat_2d(y, yrep, stat = c("q05", "q95")))
  print(bayesplot::ppc_stat_2d(y, yrep, stat = c("q01", "q99")))
  for (stat in c("q05", "q95")) {
    print(bayesplot::ppc_stat_grouped(y, yrep, group = group, stat = stat) +
            ggplot2::ggtitle(stat))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

All models are fitted with `refresh = 0` and `silent = 2`, so that the rendered report does not contain Stan's compilation and sampling messages.

The predictive checks compare the observed response with responses simulated from the model, using each person's and dataset's estimated random effects. With a Student-t likelihood, a few simulated values are extreme, and a density plot would stretch its x-axis to include them, so that the bulk of the distribution is no longer visible. The density plots are therefore zoomed to the observed range plus a margin, without dropping any simulated values, and drawn separately per benchmark model.

As a density plot cannot show well whether a model reproduces the spread and the tails, each posterior check also compares quantiles of the simulated data with the observed ones:

- The 5% and 95% quantiles describe the spread of the bulk of the distribution. They are not affected by single extreme values.
- The 1% and 99% quantiles describe the tails. This is where a Student-t likelihood should differ from a lognormal one, if the data contain outliers.
- The 5% and 95% quantiles per benchmark model show whether a misfit comes from particular models, for example from the long right tail of the idiographic VAR.

The lognormal model S1 is checked on the log scale as well, so that its checks are comparable to those of the Student-t models. The checks of S4 are not directly comparable: on the raw scale, most of the spread of log MSE is between persons, and the person random effects absorb it.


We then need to create unique identifiers for each individual, ensuring that the same id number is not mistaken as the same person across different datasets. We do this by combining the dataset name and the person id.

```{r}
#| label: create-unique-id
df_meta <- df_meta |>
  dplyr::mutate(unique_id = paste0(dataset_id, "_", id))
```

```{r}
#| label: data-relative
# the mean model is the reference (rel_mse = 1 by construction), so it is not a row here
df_rel <- df_meta |>
  dplyr::filter(set == "oos", model != "mean", is.finite(rel_mse), rel_mse > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = droplevels(model))
```

```{r}
#| label: excluded-relative
# rows without a defined relative MSE, by reason (reason_na from relative_mse() in 03)
df_meta |>
  dplyr::filter(set == "oos", model != "mean", !is.finite(rel_mse)) |>
  dplyr::count(model, reason_na) |>
  pander::pander(caption = "OOS person rows excluded from the relative MSE models.")
```

# Meta Regression for Relative MSE


## Student-t Models


### Fixed-Effect for Model, Random-Effect for Dataset (M1)
We now fit a simple meta regression model for the log relative MSE with a Student-t likelihood.

```{r}
#| label: meta-relmse-m1
model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_m1.rds")

priors_rel <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = b),
  prior(exponential(2), class = sd),
  prior(normal(-1, 1), class = b, dpar = sigma)
)
# the brms default for nu, stated so that it is reported. the lognormal S1 has no nu
priors_t <- c(priors_rel, prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = nu))

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {
  fit_relmse_m1 <- brm(
    # no intercept: the mean model is the reference and already divided out of rel_mse,
    # so each coefficient is that model's location of log relative MSE
    bf(log(rel_mse) ~ 0 + model + (1 | dataset_id) + (1 | dataset_id:model) + (1 | unique_id),
       sigma ~ 0 + model),
    data = df_rel,
    family = student(),
    prior = priors_t,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 3000,
    warmup = 1000,
    seed = seed,
    refresh = 0,
    silent = 2
  )

  saveRDS(fit_relmse_m1, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_m1 <- read_fit(model_path, "student")
}
```

These priors are:

```{r}
#| label: priors-relmse-m1
brms::prior_summary(fit_relmse_m1) |>
  dplyr::select(prior, class, coef, group) |>
  pander::pander(caption = "Priors for the Student-t meta regression model M1.")
```

```{r}
#| label: prior-predictive-m1
model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_m1_prior.rds")

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {
  fit_relmse_m1_prior <- update(fit_relmse_m1, sample_prior = "only", seed = seed,
    refresh = 0, silent = 2)
  saveRDS(fit_relmse_m1_prior, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_m1_prior <- read_fit(model_path, "student")
}

prior_check(fit_relmse_m1_prior)
```

Here's the summary of the model:
```{r}
#| label: summary-relmse-m1
parameters::model_parameters(fit_relmse_m1, test = "pd")
```

Here's a traceplot of some main parameters:

```{r}
#| label: traceplot-relmse-m1
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(fit_relmse_m1, regex_pars = "^b_")
```

Here are the posterior predictive checks of the model:

```{r}
#| label: ppcheck-relmse-m1
posterior_checks(fit_relmse_m1)
```

### M1 with Dataset-Specific Scales (M1b)

In M1, the residual scale differs only between benchmark models. Each model's errors are thus assumed to scatter equally widely in every dataset. The item-level results suggest otherwise: the idiographic VAR, for example, scatters much more in datasets with few observations per parameter. A Student-t likelihood with very small degrees of freedom ν can absorb such differences by being both very peaked and very wide. M1b therefore adds a random intercept for each combination of dataset and model to the log residual scale, so that the scales are partially pooled in the same way as the locations. The location part and all other priors are the same as in M1. The standard deviation of the new random effect gets the same prior as the other random-effect standard deviations.

If the small ν in M1 reflects such differences in scale, ν should be larger in M1b, and the predictive checks per benchmark model should fit better. If the location estimates of M1 and M1b agree, our results do not depend on how the scale is modelled.

```{r}
#| label: meta-relmse-m1b
model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_m1b.rds")

priors_t_scale <- c(priors_t, prior(exponential(2), class = sd, dpar = sigma))

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {
  fit_relmse_m1b <- brm(
    bf(log(rel_mse) ~ 0 + model + (1 | dataset_id) + (1 | dataset_id:model) + (1 | unique_id),
       sigma ~ 0 + model + (1 | dataset_id:model)),
    data = df_rel,
    family = student(),
    prior = priors_t_scale,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 3000,
    warmup = 1000,
    seed = seed,
    refresh = 0,
    silent = 2
  )

  saveRDS(fit_relmse_m1b, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_m1b <- read_fit(model_path, "student")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-relmse-m1b
parameters::model_parameters(fit_relmse_m1b, test = "pd")
```

Posterior predictive checks of M1b:

```{r}
#| label: ppcheck-relmse-m1b
posterior_checks(fit_relmse_m1b)
```

The next table compares ν between M1 and M1b, and then the location estimates of each benchmark model, as relMSE relative to the mean model. Both are posterior medians with 95% credible intervals.

```{r}
#| label: compare-m1-m1b
nu_summary <- function(fit) {
  nu <- brms::as_draws_df(fit, variable = "nu")$nu
  sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", stats::median(nu), stats::quantile(nu, 0.025),
          stats::quantile(nu, 0.975))
}

tibble::tibble(model = c("M1", "M1b"),
               nu = c(nu_summary(fit_relmse_m1), nu_summary(fit_relmse_m1b))) |>
  pander::pander(caption = "Degrees of freedom of the Student-t likelihood.")

location_summary <- function(fit) {
  location <- brms::fixef(fit, robust = TRUE)
  location <- location[grepl("^model", rownames(location)), , drop = FALSE]
  tibble::tibble(model = sub("^model", "", rownames(location)),
                 rel_mse = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", exp(location[, "Estimate"]),
                                   exp(location[, "Q2.5"]), exp(location[, "Q97.5"])))
}

dplyr::left_join(location_summary(fit_relmse_m1), location_summary(fit_relmse_m1b),
                 by = "model", suffix = c("_m1", "_m1b")) |>
  pander::pander(caption = "Population-level relMSE relative to the mean model, M1 vs. M1b.")
```


### M1 + Training Length by Model (M2)

```{r}
#| label: moderator-training-length
source(here::here("scripts", "engine", "relative.R"))
features <- readRDS(here::here("output", "analysis", "features.rds"))

# log training length split into the dataset mean (between) and the person's deviation from it (within)
train_length <- features$person |>
  dplyr::mutate(log_n = log(n_train_first)) |>
  split_between_within(log_n, dataset_id) |>
  dplyr::select(dataset_id, id, log_n_between, log_n_within)

df_rel <- dplyr::left_join(df_rel, train_length, by = c("dataset_id", "id"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(df_rel$log_n_within))
```

```{r}
#| label: meta-relmse-m2
model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_m2.rds")

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {
  fit_relmse_m2 <- brm(
    # one between and one within slope per model
    bf(log(rel_mse) ~ 0 + model + model:log_n_between + model:log_n_within +
         (1 | dataset_id) + (1 | dataset_id:model) + (1 | unique_id),
       sigma ~ 0 + model),
    data = df_rel,
    family = student(),
    prior = priors_t,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 3000,
    warmup = 1000,
    seed = seed,
    refresh = 0,
    silent = 2
  )

  saveRDS(fit_relmse_m2, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_m2 <- read_fit(model_path, "student")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prior-predictive-m2
model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_m2_prior.rds")

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {

    refresh = 0, silent = 2)

prior_check(fit_relmse_m2_prior)
```

### M2 + Autocorrelation by Model (M3)

```{r}
#| label: moderator-autocorrelation
# mean lag-1 autocorrelation of the items in the training window, split like training length
autocorrelation <- features$person |>
  dplyr::mutate(rho1 = rho1_train_mean) |>
  split_between_within(rho1, dataset_id) |>
  dplyr::select(dataset_id, id, rho1_between, rho1_within)

# rho1 is undefined for persons without observed lag pairs in the training window
df_m3 <- df_rel |>
  dplyr::left_join(autocorrelation, by = c("dataset_id", "id")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(rho1_within))
```

## Log-Normal Likelihood (S1)

```{r}

model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_s1.rds")

  fit_relmse_s1 <- brm(
    bf(rel_mse ~ 0 + model + (1 | dataset_id) + (1 | dataset_id:model) + (1 | unique_id),
       sigma ~ 0 + model),
    data = df_rel,
    family = lognormal(),
    prior = priors_rel,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 3000,
    warmup = 1000,
    seed = seed,
    refresh = 0,
    silent = 2
  )

  saveRDS(fit_relmse_s1, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_s1 <- read_fit(model_path, "lognormal")
}
```

```{r}

  fit_relmse_s1_prior <- update(fit_relmse_s1, sample_prior = "only", seed = seed,
    refresh = 0, silent = 2)
```

Posterior predictive checks of S1, on the log scale. Compared with the checks of M1, they show whether the lognormal likelihood reproduces the spread and the tails of log relative MSE as well as the Student-t likelihood does.

```{r}

posterior_checks(fit_relmse_s1, log_y = TRUE)
```

## Raw-Scale MSE (S4)

Here, we increase iterations due to some convergence issues. 

```{r}
#| label: meta-relmse-s4
model_path <- here::here("output", "analysis", "fit_relmse_s4.rds")

# all models including the mean model, so the reference is modelled instead of divided out
df_raw <- df_meta |>
  dplyr::filter(set == "oos", is.finite(gm_mse), gm_mse > 0)

# raw MSE on the [0, 1] scale is around exp(-3), not 1
priors_raw <- c(
  prior(normal(-3, 2), class = b),
  prior(exponential(2), class = sd),
  prior(normal(-1, 1), class = b, dpar = sigma),
  prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = nu)
)

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {
  fit_relmse_s4 <- brm(
    bf(log(gm_mse) ~ 0 + model + (1 | dataset_id) + (1 | dataset_id:model) + (1 | unique_id),
       sigma ~ 0 + model),
    data = df_raw,
    family = student(),
    prior = priors_raw,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 6000,
    warmup = 2000,
    seed = seed,
    refresh = 0,
    silent = 2
  )

  saveRDS(fit_relmse_s4, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_s4 <- read_fit(model_path, "student")
}
```

```{r}

if (refit_models || !file.exists(model_path)) {
  fit_relmse_s4_prior <- update(fit_relmse_s4, sample_prior = "only", seed = seed,
    refresh = 0, silent = 2)
  saveRDS(fit_relmse_s4_prior, model_path)
} else {
  fit_relmse_s4_prior <- read_fit(model_path, "student")
}

prior_check(fit_relmse_s4_prior)
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-relmse-s4
parameters::model_parameters(fit_relmse_s4, test = "pd")
```

# Convergence Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: convergence
# population-level and variance parameters only. the person-level effects are too many to list
convergence <- function(fit) {
  draws <- brms::as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b_|sd_|nu$)", regex = TRUE)
  summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(draws, "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  nuts <- brms::nuts_params(fit)
  tibble::tibble(
    max_rhat = max(summary$rhat),
    min_ess_bulk = min(summary$ess_bulk),
    min_ess_tail = min(summary$ess_tail),
    divergences = sum(nuts$Value[nuts$Parameter == "divergent__"])
  )
}

list(M1 = fit_relmse_m1, M1b = fit_relmse_m1b, M2 = fit_relmse_m2, M3 = fit_relmse_m3,
     S1 = fit_relmse_s1, S4 = fit_relmse_s4) |>
  lapply(convergence) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "model") |>
  pander::pander(digits = 3, caption = "Convergence diagnostics per fitted model.")
```

# Computation Times

Stan stores the warmup and sampling time of each chain in the fitted model, so the computation times can be read from the cached fits without refitting. They do not include the compilation of the Stan models. The four chains of a model run in parallel on separate cores: the sampling time adds up all chains, and the elapsed time is that of the slowest chain. The prior predictive models are listed separately.

```{r}
#| label: meta-times
meta_fits <- list(
  M1 = fit_relmse_m1, M1b = fit_relmse_m1b, M2 = fit_relmse_m2, M3 = fit_relmse_m3,
  S1 = fit_relmse_s1, S4 = fit_relmse_s4,
  `M1 prior` = fit_relmse_m1_prior, `M2 prior` = fit_relmse_m2_prior,
  `M3 prior` = fit_relmse_m3_prior, `S1 prior` = fit_relmse_s1_prior,
  `S4 prior` = fit_relmse_s4_prior
)

# seconds per chain, one column each for warmup and sampling
meta_times <- lapply(meta_fits, function(fit) {
  chain_sec <- rstan::get_elapsed_time(fit$fit)
  tibble::tibble(chains = nrow(chain_sec), sampling_sec = sum(chain_sec),
                 elapsed_sec = max(rowSums(chain_sec)))
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "model") |>
  dplyr::mutate(prior_only = grepl("prior$", model))

meta_times |>
  dplyr::mutate(sampling_min = sampling_sec / 60, elapsed_min = elapsed_sec / 60) |>
  dplyr::select(model, chains, sampling_min, elapsed_min) |>
  pander::pander(digits = 3, caption = "Sampling time of the meta-models in minutes.")

meta_with_data <- dplyr::filter(meta_times, !prior_only)
slowest_meta <- dplyr::slice_max(meta_with_data, elapsed_sec, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

Sampling the `r nrow(meta_with_data)` meta-models with data took `r sprintf("%.0f", sum(meta_with_data$sampling_sec) / 60)` minutes in total, summed over all chains, and `r sprintf("%.0f", sum(meta_with_data$elapsed_sec) / 60)` minutes of elapsed time when the models are fitted one after another with parallel chains. The slowest model was `r slowest_meta$model` (`r sprintf("%.0f", slowest_meta$elapsed_sec / 60)` minutes elapsed). The prior predictive models added `r sprintf("%.0f", sum(meta_times$sampling_sec[meta_times$prior_only]) / 60)` minutes of sampling time.
